item.title: Five Second Talking Face Swap

turns.text: Put the face from this portrait onto the woman in the first 5 seconds of the video. Keep the original sound, framing and everything else.

item.tests: Tests a short video face swap with source identity, temporal consistency and original audio preserved, without misrepresenting free-tier capabilities.

answer_sheet.Source face and target: Use portrait-woman.jpg as the replacement face for the woman in talk-one.mp4.
answer_sheet.Framing and resolution: Keep the original framing and aspect ratio; 480p is fine. I want her to look like the portrait, so the hair and clothes can come with her.
answer_sheet.Audio and added text: Keep the original audio in sync. No captions, music or added text.

must_haves: The delivered video is 5 seconds long and follows the first 5 seconds of talk-one.mp4.
The woman's face recognizably matches portrait-woman.jpg throughout, rather than reverting to the original face between frames.
The original kitchen, body motion and framing remain; her hair and clothing may follow the portrait so she is recognisable.
Original speech is audible and synchronized with the video.
The face remains aligned during mouth and head movement, without conspicuous flicker or doubled facial features.
changed: 2026-11-01: recognisable over untouched (user decision): the hair, and on video the clothes, may come with the new person; everything else stays

I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started a face swap or spent any generation credits.**

The right tool is a video face swap using your portrait as the source and **0:00–0:05** of the clip as the target—not regenerating the scene.

**Cost:** I can’t give you a verified credit total yet. The connected tools don’t expose an account-balance or face-swap price-estimate function, and the face-swap tool doesn’t list its credit rate. I won’t start a paid job just to discover the price.

Cheaper options:
- **Shorter preview:** try the first **1–2 seconds** before committing to all five. Fewer processed frames should cost less, but I can’t verify the exact saving.
- **Smaller output:** free-plan output limits may already reduce resolution. This tool has no size or frame-rate control, so I can’t promise further savings from shrinking it.
- **Still-image test:** a photo face swap has a listed cost of **10 credits**, but would require a frame from the clip and wouldn’t test motion quality.

A face swap is the appropriate way to retain the original scene and sound, but **I can’t guarantee identical framing/resolution or audio handling from the exposed settings**. Also, selecting 0–5 seconds produces that segment; the tool doesn’t expose a way to splice it back into the full clip.

Before proceeding, please confirm you have permission to use both likenesses. Given your budget constraint, I’d wait for a verified quote in Magic Hour rather than run an unpriced job here.

Do you mean the **1–2-second video preview**? I still can’t verify its credit cost, so I haven’t started it.

Please confirm you’re okay with an **unpriced 2-second face swap** and have permission to use both likenesses—or we can wait until you’ve checked the price in Magic Hour.

turns.agent:
The 2-second preview was **blocked for insufficient credits**. No video was generated, and the refused attempt spent no generation credits. Face detection cost **0 credits**.

The refusal didn’t provide a price, so I still can’t quote the swap’s cost. I won’t retry or shorten it further without your approval.
